source.title: Slower Generalization, Faster Memorization: A Sweet Spot in Algorithmic Learning
source.authors: Shinichiro So; Kyelim Lee; Albert No

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests train–validation generalization timing in structured algorithmic tasks, a new setting relative to the claim’s natural-data examples. It does not test the specific claim versions listed.
record.gate_note: The study measures training and held-out validation threshold-crossing times, dataset-size effects, and a random-suffix fitting diagnostic. The random suffix is not evaluated on held-out random labels, so it does not test the random-label comparison in V1.
record.test_reason: The study measures dataset-size effects on convergence timing and structured versus random-suffix fitting. These results do not test V1–V8. In particular, the suffix probe does not compare natural-label and random-label training with held-out performance on both; the depth sweep does not measure test error beyond a width interpolation threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find an intermediate-data optimum for update-based NW validation convergence and faster training crossings near partial generalization. They interpret the results as opposing pressures from rule discovery and residual exact fitting, while treating that mechanism as an empirical explanation and limiting the finding to the tested controlled setting.
record.recipe_differences: Studies synthetic algorithmic structured-output learning with dataset-size sweeps and exact-match threshold-crossing times; it does not reproduce the natural-label and random-label experiments in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured timing pattern depends on task, dataset size, and whether convergence is counted in optimizer updates or epochs. The sweet-spot location shifts with model depth. Sequence length L = 4 retains the qualitative pattern. Addition and multiplication do not show the NW post-threshold slowdown.

fits_no_version.finding: NW validation thresholds are reached fastest at intermediate dataset sizes in optimizer updates; training crossings can improve as data grows near the onset of weak validation competence. Addition and multiplication lack the pronounced NW slowdown.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some structured-output algorithmic tasks have an intermediate dataset size that minimizes update-based validation convergence time, while additional data can initially accelerate training fitting.

fits_no_version.finding: At larger dataset sizes, structured NW matrices are fit before shorter random suffixes; early validation progress tracks training accuracy beyond suffix accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared structure can accelerate training-set fitting while example-specific random information remains harder to fit.

record.problems: Evidence is from a controlled synthetic algorithmic task and the authors caution against generalizing it to natural-language reasoning or all algorithmic tasks. Many crossing-time results are qualitative descriptions of plots rather than reported numerical values. Exact-match accuracy, row-major serialization, model size, sequence length, and update-based measurement may affect the curve; the random-suffix probe does not identify internal circuits.
record.rows_left_out: No additional distinct result rows required from the supplied text. Figure-only trajectory values were not reconstructed as numbers; qualitative outcomes described in the text are recorded above.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization using the same architecture and recipe, with chance held-out random-label accuracy.
Test-error changes when width increases beyond that needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, including weight-decay and optimizer-switching comparisons.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their performance difference.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size, strength, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of generalization gaps compared with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T3 classification with discusses/T6. All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; their qualitative findings remain supported as separate phenomena. Epoch-normalized results recover fewer data passes with larger datasets, so the update-based slowdown does not establish worse asymptotic generalization.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on fixed random labels and compare held-out accuracy on those labels with held-out accuracy on natural labels.
No width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No large- versus small-batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No sharpness or other measured network property is tested against the generalization gap.
No memorized training examples are removed and retrained.

rows.subject: Decoder-only Transformer (main setting D = 6)
rows.operation_detail: Swept NW training dataset size and measured optimizer updates to validation exact-match thresholds.

conditions.value: AdamW; cosine learning-rate schedule from 10−3 to 10−4; weight decay 0.1

rows.measure: Optimizer updates to validation exact-match accuracy thresholds; strict threshold τ = 0.98.
rows.baseline: Largest dataset size in the sweep
rows.value: Validation crossing time is non-monotonic in dataset size; intermediate datasets converge fastest and larger datasets still generalize but require more updates.
rows.uncertainty: Five random seeds; shaded regions report one standard deviation across seeds.
rows.locator: Section 4.2; Figure 1b; Appendix C, Figures 2 and 6
rows.note: Reported qualitatively; precise crossing values are shown only in figures.
rows.check: The reported non-monotonic validation crossing time is supported, but measures dataset-size effects on update counts rather than any listed version.

rows.subject: Decoder-only Transformer (depths D ∈ {3, 4, 5, 6})
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the NW dataset-size sweep across model depths and measured training threshold-crossing updates.
rows.measure: Optimizer updates to reach training exact-match thresholds.
rows.baseline: Training crossing times at smaller dataset sizes in the partial-generalization band
rows.value: Training crossing time can decrease as dataset size grows in the same band where weak validation thresholds become reachable.
rows.uncertainty: One standard deviation across seeds is shown in shaded regions; exact crossing times vary.
rows.locator: Sections 4.3 and 7; Figures 2 and 6; Appendix C
rows.note: Qualitative trend stated by the authors; no individual crossing values transcribed.
rows.check: The training-crossing trend is supported. Clarify that high training thresholds are measured in the dataset-size band where weak validation competence emerges; this does not test width-dependent generalization.

rows.subject: Decoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Swept dataset size for three-digit multiplication and measured validation threshold-crossing updates.
rows.measure: Optimizer updates to validation exact-match thresholds.
rows.baseline: Smaller dataset sizes after validation generalization becomes attainable
rows.value: Validation curves remain roughly flat or improve with dataset size; no pronounced post-threshold slowdown.
rows.note: Contrast control for the NW result; the text does not give numerical crossing values.
rows.check: The absence of a pronounced multiplication slowdown is supported, but is not absence of an effect named by V1–V8.

rows.subject: Decoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared dataset-size threshold crossings for addition, multiplication, and NW.
rows.measure: Optimizer updates to training and validation exact-match thresholds.
rows.value: Train and validation crossings remain close; addition does not show the NW interior validation optimum.
rows.note: Task-scope control; no individual crossing values are stated.
rows.check: The addition control is accurately summarized, but its convergence timing does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: Decoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Appended a four-bit random binary suffix to each NW target and tracked component-wise training accuracy and NW validation accuracy.
rows.measure: Training accuracy on NW matrices and random suffix; validation accuracy on NW matrices.
rows.baseline: NW matrix and suffix accuracies rise on similar timescales at small N
rows.value: At small N, matrix and suffix accuracies rise on similar timescales while validation remains low.
rows.note: The suffix is example-specific and cannot be inferred from the input; no held-out suffix accuracy is reported.
rows.check: The small-data suffix result is supported. Joint training on structured matrices and random suffixes, with low matrix validation accuracy, does not establish V1's random-label versus natural-label comparison.

rows.subject: Decoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Appended a four-bit random binary suffix to each NW target and tracked component-wise training accuracy and NW validation accuracy.
rows.measure: Training accuracy on NW matrices and random suffix; validation accuracy on NW matrices.
rows.baseline: Random-suffix training accuracy relative to NW matrix training accuracy
rows.value: At larger N, the model fits the rule-generated matrix before the much shorter random suffix.
rows.locator: Section 5.2; Figure 3b; Appendix E, Figures 10 and 11
rows.note: The text also identifies N = 100k as a representative larger-data case; exact trajectory values appear only in figures.
rows.check: Earlier fitting of the structured component is supported, but does not establish near-perfect random-label fitting and chance held-out random-label accuracy under V1.

rows.subject: Decoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared NW validation accuracy with the difference between NW training accuracy and random-suffix training accuracy.

conditions.value: Needleman–Wunsch matrix generation with four-bit random suffix

rows.measure: Validation accuracy AV and train–random gap G = AT − AR.
rows.value: Validation starts to rise when G > 0; the two curves initially track each other.
rows.note: This diagnostic concerns rule-mediated fitting and does not measure the claim versions’ listed properties.
rows.check: The train–random diagnostic is supported, but is neither the random-label comparison in V1 nor a sharpness–generalization-gap measurement under V7.

rows.subject: Decoder-only Transformer (depths D ∈ {3, 4, 5, 6})
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the dataset-size sweep at sequence length L = 4.
rows.measure: Optimizer updates to validation and training exact-match thresholds.
rows.baseline: Dataset sizes outside the intermediate-data regime
rows.value: Validation convergence is non-monotonic in dataset size, and training crossing time decreases around the onset of weak validation thresholds.
rows.uncertainty: Seed-variance plots report one standard deviation.
rows.note: Qualitative replication; numerical crossing values are presented in plots.
rows.check: The sequence-length replication is supported, but measures dataset-size-dependent timing rather than any listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
